{quote}Hello Team,

We previously discussed this matter with Local OPS, the GM at that time, and Legal; however, I no longer have access to the [*original ticket*|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/47/LSS-36533][ |https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/47/LSS-36533]and the email thread I still have is incomplete. Because of this, we may need to revisit the topic. In Romania, for at least three years, we have been aligned with Local OPS — the final authority regarding suppliers — that accounts blocked for fraudulent activities must not be deleted, and that we do not inform drivers about deletion requests in such cases. Doing so would create both a precedent and legal implications for us.

*Why would it set a precedent?* If we inform a suspended fraudulent driver that their account has been deleted, they can pass this information to other fraudulent drivers, encouraging them to request deletions as well, hoping to open a new account afterward.

*Why would it create legal issues?* Since we are _not actually deleting_ such accounts, if the same driver later submits a new registration and gets rejected, they will question the reason for the rejection. We would not be able to disclose that the account was never deleted in the first place and there will be cases, in which OS will be providing this information either due to lack of knowledge or because they do not understand our processes.

For these reasons, we use the following response template provided by the Privacy Team:

"_Va multumim pentru rabdarea acordata._ _Va aducem in vedere faptul ca dumneavoastra aveti dreptul sa ne solicitati stergerea datelor dumneavoastra in anumite circumstante, totusi dreptul de a fi uitat nu este unul absolut. In acest caz, nu am putut da curs solicitarii dumneavoastra de stergere a datelor intrucat contul dumneavoastra a fost suspendat. Astfel dorim sa ne asiguram ca nu folositi dreptul de a fi uitat in mod ilegitim, pentru a va crea un alt cont de sofer cu scopul de a evita blocarea._ _Este specificat de asemenea in Politica de confidențialitate aplicabilă Șoferilor ca datele dumneavoastra cu caracter personal vor fi stocate atâta timp cât dețineți un cont activ de șofer. Dacă vi se închide contul atunci datele dvs. cu caracter personal vor fi stocate pentru o perioadă suplimentară de 3 ani. Datele de care este nevoie în scopuri contabile vor fi stocate timp de 7 ani. În cazul în care există suspiciuni privind infracțiuni, fraude sau furnizare de informații false, datele vor fi stocate timp de 10 ani._ _Va multumim pentru intelegere si va stam la dispozitie pentru orice alte intrebari sau nelamuriri._ _Cu stima"_

Please consult with the Privacy Team on this. Much appreciated!

+*BACKGROUND*+

* In April, a teleperformance agent altered the bank details of a UK driver ([profile|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fleet/drivers/edit/2315801?tab=profile&filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn]). The driver has not received any payments from Bolt since that date - however the payments have left and not bounced back.
** The bank details currently on the driver’s account do not match any bank statements we have on file for him. As such, the reporter (Ops) believes we have added the wrong driver’s bank details.
* Driver only reported this issue on {{2025-12-15}}
* Apparently, the driver has since been informed that they will be paid.
** Bank details have also been reverted to what they were in April 2025.

+*ANALYSIS*+

* It sounds like the incident is no longer ongoing, so no additional _immediate_ mitigation steps are needed. However, we still need to get to the root cause of why this happened, so that the TP agent does not do this again.

Hey,

In Malta we have commission netting.

_Through commission netting, your campaigns/bonuses/compensations are reflected as a discount from your commission, instead of each having their individual invoices. Simply, your commission is reduced in the amount of your campaigns/bonuses/compensations - ensuring a more clear invoicing process, and less invoicing noise._

_For example, previously you would see a commission of 416.91€ and separate bonus lines of 11€ on your invoice, which totaled up to 361.92€. Now, you would only see a single row of commission in the amount of 361.92€, meaning the calculation is already done in the background._



Example for some [Driver|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fleet/drivers/edit/3318350?tab=profile&filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn]:

Taking November 2025 example from [Balance history|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/billing-rides/balanceHistory?balanceHistoryFilterSearch=%7B%22external_id%22%3A3318350%2C%22type%22%3A%22Driver%22%2C%22month%22%3A%7B%22month%22%3A11%2C%22year%22%3A2025%7D%2C%22viewType%22%3A%22monthly%22%2C%22week%22%3A%7B%22start%22%3A1762725600000%2C%22end%22%3A1763330399999%7D%7D]. 

Commission that driver had to pay is

{quote}*Commission = expense_cash_commission* + *expense_commission* (48.50 EUR + 190.83 EUR) = €239.33 EUR{quote}

this commission is ±20% of the amount driver had in Ride fees

{quote}Fees = *earning_in_app_ride_fee* + *earning_cash_ride_fee* (947.70 EUR + 242.50 EUR) = €1,190.20 EUR

Commission % = commission / fees = €239.33 EUR / 1,190.20 EUR = 0.20 = 20%{quote}

the [invoice|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/billing-document/invoices/5649895597?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] was issued for 132.94 euro, which is less than 239.33 because we do *commission netting* in Estonia.

{quote}*What is Commission Netting?*

*Commission netting* is a process used to simplify how drivers are invoiced for commissions, especially when there are bonuses, campaigns, or compensations involved.

*Without Netting:*

Normally, a driver would receive separate invoices:

One for the commission they owe (e.g., 20% of ride fees)

Separate invoices for any bonuses, campaigns, or compensations they receive

*With Netting (as done in Estonia):*

Instead of issuing multiple invoices, the system *reduces the commission amount* by the total value of any bonuses, campaigns, or compensations the driver earned.

The driver receives a *single, lower commission invoice* that already accounts for these discounts.{quote}

You can see discounts earned via cash and app rides in *earning_cash_discount_netted* and *earning_in_app_discount_netted.*

So we can calculate the final netted commission like this:

{quote}Netted Commission = Commission - *earning_cash_discount_netted - earning_in_app_discount_netted* = €239.33 - 26.70 EUR - 79.70 EUR = €132.93{quote}

132.93 is the same amount you can see on Monthly invoice (take invoice from November from [+here+|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/billing-rides/clients/128179276?tab=partner_invoices&filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn])

✨ That’s how you can calculate Commission Netting in Balance history.

Nikolay Roll

There is an issue on the Finish Ride screen when navigating to the Subscriptions list. Navigation is currently handled via a URL-based action while the app is already open, which causes *unexpected behaviors in the Android navigation stack*. For in-app navigation, predefined actions should be used instead of deep links.

The proposed solution is to use the *action type* {{"subscriptions"}} instead of a URL. This action type is supported in the RFC and already used in other flows. Hello, Olha! Thank you for your reply. We will review this with the team and assess the best way to approach this request. 



When it comes to your question about FIRR, customer support does not use FIRR at all at the moment as far as I know. FIRR also does not specify how effective the first solution was, because interaction is just one instance of handling time. There could be multiple small periods of handling times happening before an actual resolution is provided from our side. However, reopen rate shows whether the support case was re-opened after being moved to Solved or not, which is a much more realistic way of seeing whether the first solution was good or not.

Thank you for your patience while we investigated your case.

Our records show that your Bolt account associated with the phone number ending with 2341 was recently accessed by another user. This happened because your old account was still linked to that phone number, which has since been reassigned by your mobile operator. This can sometimes occur when operators recycle numbers that are no longer in use. Bolt users may log into their account via their phone number. If a user does not enable two-factor authentication (‘2FA’) in the Bolt App nor updates their phone number in the Bolt App after changing it, and their old phone number is later reassigned by the mobile provider to a new customer, that new customer may inadvertently gain access to the existing Bolt account linked to it. This situation may occur if the new customer attempts to register a new account or requests a one-time password (‘OTP’) to a phone number previously owned by an account holder.

Please note that, in accordance with our terms and conditions available at: [Terms and Conditions|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/] , you must inform us of any update in your contact details, including phone number changes, at the earliest opportunity. This ensures the continued security of your Bolt account and prevents similar situations from occurring. If you’d like to continue using Bolt, please create a new account using your current phone number.

To protect your data and ensure proper access control, the account in question will now be permanently archived. Once archived, neither you nor the new number owner will be able to access its details, data, or history.

To help keep your new account secure going forward, please ensure that:

* Your phone number linked to the account is up to date;
* Your email address linked to the account is verified; and
* You enable multi-factor authentication via_“My account > Log in and security > Turn on Two-Step Verification”_;
* You never share your passkey, or OTP codes received via SMS with anyone.

If you notice any suspicious activity in your account in the future, or receive an email about a new device login, please contact our Customer Support Team immediately.

Best regards,

Bolt Customer Support

h3. Driver’s payout is smaller than the ending balance they had on Sunday

*If the Driver reports that they received less than the reported amount:*

* This can happen if last weeks balance is higher than their current balance. Payouts are done with either last weeks balance or their current balance, whichever is smaller. This is done to avoid partner balance turning negative after payout.
* Advise the Driver that regular weekly payouts are generated according to their available balance at the moment when the payout is created. If it is less than what was reported by the end of the previous week, they most likely had deductions on their balance, such as an early cashout, new cash orders (accumulating commission) or other fees charged. This is done to prevent their balance from going negative.
** You can check this by going to *Billing, Billing Rides, Billing History*, and search for the Driver ID and the respective week.
** Compare the 'Balance before' amount and check the 'payout' amount under 'Total earnings and expenses for period' section
** *If the payout was smaller than the ending balance of the previous week:* It's because of deductions on their balance, such as an early cashout, new cash orders (accumulating commission) or other fees charged.

Hey,

In Romania we have commission netting.

_Through commission netting, your campaigns/bonuses/compensations are reflected as a discount from your commission, instead of each having their individual invoices. Simply, your commission is reduced in the amount of your campaigns/bonuses/compensations - ensuring a more clear invoicing process, and less invoicing noise._

_For example, previously you would see a commission of 416.91€ and separate bonus lines of 11€ on your invoice, which totaled up to 361.92€. Now, you would only see a single row of commission in the amount of 361.92€, meaning the calculation is already done in the background._



Example for some [Driver|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fleet/drivers/edit/3318350?tab=profile&filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn]:

Taking November 2025 example from [Balance history|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/billing-rides/balanceHistory?balanceHistoryFilterSearch=%7B%22external_id%22%3A3318350%2C%22type%22%3A%22Driver%22%2C%22month%22%3A%7B%22month%22%3A11%2C%22year%22%3A2025%7D%2C%22viewType%22%3A%22monthly%22%2C%22week%22%3A%7B%22start%22%3A1762725600000%2C%22end%22%3A1763330399999%7D%7D]. 

Commission that driver had to pay is

{quote}*Commission = expense_cash_commission* + *expense_commission* (48.50 EUR + 190.83 EUR) = €239.33 EUR{quote}

this commission is ±20% of the amount driver had in Ride fees

{quote}Fees = *earning_in_app_ride_fee* + *earning_cash_ride_fee* (947.70 EUR + 242.50 EUR) = €1,190.20 EUR

Commission % = commission / fees = €239.33 EUR / 1,190.20 EUR = 0.20 = 20%{quote}

the [invoice|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/billing-document/invoices/5649895597?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] was issued for 132.94 euro, which is less than 239.33 because we do *commission netting* in Estonia.

{quote}*What is Commission Netting?*

*Commission netting* is a process used to simplify how drivers are invoiced for commissions, especially when there are bonuses, campaigns, or compensations involved.

*Without Netting:*

Normally, a driver would receive separate invoices:

One for the commission they owe (e.g., 20% of ride fees)

Separate invoices for any bonuses, campaigns, or compensations they receive

*With Netting (as done in Estonia):*

Instead of issuing multiple invoices, the system *reduces the commission amount* by the total value of any bonuses, campaigns, or compensations the driver earned.

The driver receives a *single, lower commission invoice* that already accounts for these discounts.{quote}

You can see discounts earned via cash and app rides in *earning_cash_discount_netted* and *earning_in_app_discount_netted.*

So we can calculate the final netted commission like this:

{quote}Netted Commission = Commission - *earning_cash_discount_netted - earning_in_app_discount_netted* = €239.33 - 26.70 EUR - 79.70 EUR = €132.93{quote}

132.93 is the same amount you can see on Monthly invoice (take invoice from November from [+here+|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/billing-rides/clients/128179276?tab=partner_invoices&filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn])

✨ That’s how you can calculate Commission Netting in Balance history.

Advise the customer to *check with their bank* to confirm the release of the preauthorisation. Banks handle these releases differently, and while some are immediate, others may process it as a temporary charge that is then refunded. Sometimes, the payment is reversed without the bank sending a reversal notification to the customer, which might lead the user to think that the reversal has not been made.

The reversal can take up to *30 days* to complete, as pending authorisations typically expire after that time on banks end.

Unfortunately, we don't have full visibility into all the parties involved in the payment processing beyond our payment partner. Therefore, we can't track the exact status of the preauthorisation release once it has been sent.

Hi Sigrid, 

* _the complete history report of the scooter for the duration of my ride_

CSV is sufficient for DSAR compliance, because it covers all personal data about their use of the scooter during their trip. It does not have to include the vehicle’s maintenance or operational history outside the ride, unless that history contains personal data relating to the requester (which is almost never the case). We should address this point as follows:

_We have provided all personal data generated during your ride, including vehicle telemetry, event logs and relevant technical indicators. This constitutes all personal data we hold that relates to your use of the scooter for that ride. The full historical technical data of the scooter outside your trip is not considered your personal data and therefore does not fall within the scope of the right of access._

* _access to the technical data that are supposed to prove that there were no problems_

Under GDPR, we must provide personal data, not internal assessments or technical reasoning unless they contain personal data. We can provide any system health indicators during the ride captured _during the user’s ride_ (if available), but not maintenance logs outside the ride. Has Ops previously checked this information? 

* _the contact details of the Stel (person who can provide this information)_

We should address this as follows:
_To protect the privacy of our employees, we cannot share individual staff members’ personal contact details. Our Privacy team handles all requests relating to personal data, and you may continue to direct any DSAR-related questions to:_ [_privacy@bolt.eu_|mailto:privacy@bolt.eu] _or through Customer Support team._

Bolt must therefore cooperate by providing only basic administrative data (existence of the account, date of creation, contact details and mandatory legal documents like driver’s license or insurance card etc).

However, sensitive or intrusive data such as complete ride history, geolocation, schedules, remuneration amounts or bank details cannot be transmitted upon simple administrative request. Their communication requires a court order, in accordance with the GDPR and the principle of minimisation.

h2. Dear Contracting Authority / Review Committee,

We hereby submit a formal challenge concerning several provisions contained in the procurement documentation. After a thorough legal and practical assessment, we find that certain technical and qualification requirements are not proportionate, restrict competition in an unjustified manner, and may not align with the principles and objectives of the Public Procurement Act (RHS). We respectfully request that the contracting authority review, amend, or provide adequate justification for these requirements to ensure compliance with RHS § 3, § 4, and § 89.

First, the requirement to use a physical taximeter and taximeter printer, together with a mandatory taximeter-based pricing structure, appears unnecessarily restrictive. Bolt Business provides fully transparent, verifiable digital trip records through certified electronic logs and electronic invoicing. All data elements required for oversight—time, distance, route, pricing components—are presented in a traceable, audit-ready format. Because the contracting authority’s stated goal of ensuring transparent trip documentation can be met by modern technological solutions, limiting acceptable methods exclusively to a physical taximeter is not proportionate within the meaning of RHS § 89(1). Such a requirement excludes equally effective solutions without a valid technical necessity.

Second, the obligation for the tenderer to have at least 50 vehicles registered for taxi service (with corresponding taxi service vehicle cards) unjustifiably narrows the pool of eligible providers. Platform-based mobility providers operate through licensed partners rather than owning large vehicle fleets directly, yet they are capable of ensuring service availability, adequate fleet capacity, and high operational reliability. The contracting authority’s legitimate objectives—service accessibility, sufficient vehicle volume, and continuity—could be achieved through alternative, non-discriminatory mechanisms such as response-time criteria, service-level agreements, or aggregate partner capacity. As formulated, the requirement restricts competition and conflicts with the principle of promoting competition under RHS § 3(2).

Third, the procurement has been framed strictly as a taxi service within the legal meaning of taxi legislation, requiring a taxi service vehicle card, driver service card, and taximeter. This classification presumes that the contracting authority requires traditional, street-hail taxi operations. However, the described use case suggests a need for pre-ordered transport services supported by clear invoicing. If the authority’s substantive needs do not require strict adherence to taxi legislation, then mandating all elements of taxi service regulation may be inconsistent with the purposefulness principle set out in RHS § 4(1). An overly narrow definition of the service type risks excluding modern, pre-booked mobility solutions capable of fulfilling the authority’s functional requirements.

Fourth, the obligation to issue a physical printed receipt is technically outdated and disproportionate. The digital receipts issued by Bolt Business contain all required information—timestamps, distance, pricing, route details—and are stored in a manner that ensures verifiability and traceability. In accordance with RHS § 89(1), technical specifications must not unnecessarily hinder the use of alternative technological solutions where these achieve the same result. Since a physical printout does not add value beyond that provided by a secure digital record, the requirement is excessively rigid.

Finally, the procurement documentation mandates a strict tariff-based pricing model tied to taximeter calculations. This excludes pricing models that offer the contracting authority potentially superior predictability, stability, and administrative simplicity, such as fixed pricing or pre-calculated fares. Restricting acceptable pricing formats to one legacy model is not aligned with the broader purpose of ensuring cost-effective and efficient procurement and may conflict with the proportionality principle under RHS § 4(1).

In light of the above, we conclude that the procurement documentation, as currently formulated, imposes requirements that are not proportionate, unnecessarily restrict competition, and exclude innovative, technologically advanced service models capable of fulfilling the contracting authority’s functional needs. We respectfully request that the contracting authority:

# *Review and amend the contested provisions* to allow alternative, functionally equivalent solutions, or
# *Provide detailed justification demonstrating the necessity and proportionality* of the requirements under applicable provisions of the Public Procurement Act.

We remain available to provide any additional explanations or information the contracting authority may require.

*Dear Product Team,*

I have raised this request on the 10th October, with a productive follow-up call with [~accountid:5f23e228bedd1000153843ae]  and re-raising with the below information due to the deal approaching completion date. This request on behalf of a high-potential prospective client in the aviation sector, with an expected annualized GMV impact of *€100K–250K*. 

*Salesforce Opp:* [Aviation Services Handling Limited|https://bolt-eu.lightning.force.com/lightning/r/Opportunity/006P400000b8fNJIAY/view]

h3. Client and Opportunity

The prospect is an aviation services company based at Malta International Airport (Skyparks Business Centre area). They are actively engaging with us and have indicated a strong intent to close the deal by *January 2026*. Securing this account would represent significant growth.

h3. Current Limitation

In Bolt Business, the "Ride locations" policy – specifically the "*To or from certain locations*" option (which restricts rides to/from defined points, e.g., the airport or office) – *currently prevents the completion of a ride booking if multiple stops are added* when using a business payment method tied to this policy.

This restriction limits the policy's practical use for scenarios requiring shared rides with intermediate drop-offs.

h3. Client Use Case

The client needs to enforce rides *to/from the airport* (their primary hub) while allowing employees to share vehicles efficiently. A common scenario is:

* A group of employees departs from the same starting point (e.g., airport after a shift or office).
* They share one vehicle, with the driver making multiple stops to drop off each employee at their individual home addresses, or work (the airport).

This promotes cost savings, reduces the number of vehicles needed, and supports sustainability goals by minimizing trips. Without the ability to add multiple stops, employees would need to book separate rides, {color:#bf2600}significantly increasing costs for our client and administrative overhead for the client.{color}

h3. Fraud Concern and Proposed Mitigation

I understand the primary reason for the current limitation is to prevent potential fraud, where a user could add unauthorized stops (including a restricted one) to bypass the policy.

However, responsibility for monitoring and preventing misuse ultimately lies with the client administrator and their employees. Many corporate clients already manage similar risks in other expense categories successfully.

{color:#006644}*To address this proactively while enabling the feature:*{color}

* Introduce an *optional toggle* in the Bolt Business Dashboard allowing administrators to enable multiple stops when using the "To or from certain locations" policy.
* When enabling this option, display a *prominent caution notice*, such as: _"Note: Enabling multiple stops may allow users to add intermediate destinations. Administrators are recommended to regularly review ride details and enforce internal approval processes to ensure compliance with company policy."_

This approach empowers clients with flexibility, clearly communicates the shared responsibility, and maintains safeguards without overly restricting legitimate use cases.

h3. Business Impact

Approving and implementing this enhancement would directly unblock this high-value deal and position Bolt Business more competitively against platforms that offer similar flexibility in location-based policies. It would also open doors to additional aviation and shift-based corporate clients with comparable needs.

Please let me know if you need any further details. 

I believe this is a low-risk, high-reward improvement that aligns with our goal of delivering maximum value to enterprise customers.

{quote}And why should we communicate 23%? I.e. the total commission is 27.8%, and yes this includes VAT, but so do many other services. I don't see why we would communicate it without VAT{quote}

The total shown (27.8%) includes VAT, but that does not mean our commission is 27.8%. Commission and VAT are two different things:
• Commission (23%) is what Bolt charges drivers.
• VAT (4.8%) is what Bolt remits to the tax authorities.
Drivers can reclaim the 4.8% VAT, so the actual commission for them remains 23%, not 27.8%.

*Context:*
We recently transitioned from the Estonian entity (Bolt Ops OÜ) to the local Dutch entity. As a result, VAT on commission is no longer reversed. Importantly, this does *not* change the bottom-line cost for drivers. Communicating that our commission is 27.8% is therefore incorrect.

Unfortunately, due to earlier communications suggesting a 27.8% commission, some drivers now believe we increased our commission rate. This has escalated to calls for a boycott and even personal threats toward me. The reality is that nothing changed in terms of what drivers pay,  the only change is that the local entity is now the billing operator instead of the Estonian entity, which is why VAT appears differently.

+*UPDATE (16.12)*+

*EXTERNAL COUNSEL DISCUSSION*

* Kristiina Taube asked KVDL on 25 November to following Q: In connection to PSD2, would AML/KYC compliance obligations applicable to a regulated payment or e-money institution prevail over privacy law restrictions re collecting BSNs?
* Key points from KVDL’s advice were as follows:
** Bolt is *not required to collect and store BSN*, so likely not allowed.
*** “_According to DNB, there’s no obligation for a financial institution to record the BSN when performing CDD under the Dutch AML/CFT Act_”.
*** “_Sometimes a financial enterprise needs the BSN for reporting purposes, i.e. to the Dutch Tax Authorities. The financial enterprise may then request and store the BSN for this purpose. Banks for example have such reporting obligations. As far as we know, Payment Institutions and E-money institutions do not have such reporting obligations. In such case, we assume storing the BSN does not serve any statutory obligation and would therefore not be allowed_”.
*** NB. AML POC separately stated “_the practice of accepting a full copy ID and later for storage purposes shielding certain data on the copy stored, does not seem to be common practice in AML compliance_” ([link|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C05NYVA7T2A/p1765366731685649?thread_ts=1765364265.807489&cid=C05NYVA7T2A]). This seems to be the current rationale for not reacting BSN.
** However, *Bolt may still need to collect full copies of IDs* to check authenticity (but can then subsequently apply redactions).
*** Dutch DP authority states that data subjects “_may not shield any data on the copy ID yourself. And [they] may not put a watermark on it either. Otherwise the bank cannot check the authenticity of your ID. After (re)identification, your bank can shield data on the copy ID or add a watermark to it to protect your personal data_”. See [here|https://www.autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl/en/themes/finances/financial-enterprises/identification-at-financial-enterprises#is-my-bank-allowed-to-make-or-ask-for-a-copy-id].
* Having discussed with Kristiina ([here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/D0A4HJYQB24/p1765882123695099]), KVDL are quite expensive. However, we can send follow-ups if needed.
** NB. KVDL’s advice focused on financial institutions (not current processing), so follow-up Qs should focus on the former if possible.
* THOUGHTS / NEXT STEPS:
** Await Kristiina confirm re invoice setup with external counsel.
** Check the following with external counsel:
*** You have previously stated: (i) that there is no obligation for financial institutions to record BSN in the context of CDD under the Dutch AML/CFT Act (Wwft); but (ii) as part of CDD checks, financial institutions can request full copies of ID (which includes BSN). To be clear - will this continue to be the case under PSD3 (and its local implementation on the Netherlands)? Will PSD3 give Bolt a legal basis to *_collect_* BSNs?
*** Do either current AML/KYC laws in the Netherlands or PSD3 give Bolt a legal basis to *_retain_* BSNs once checks are complete (since Bolt is not legally required to store it for tax reporting purposes)? If not, is the expectation that Bolt must subsequently redact the BSN once the checks are complete? You mentioned this was a grey area and could explore in more detail.
** CONCLUSION:
*** Bolt can justify initial collection of BSN once it is a financial institution (as it needs a full copy of the ID without redaction), but once checks are passed it sounds like it is difficult to justify continued retention.
*** As such, we can continue asking for the back of IDs. But in 2026, we need to consider solutions for subsequent redaction.

*BSN EXTRACTION*

* BSN is no longer automatically extracted and listed on driver profiles ([here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C05NYVA7T2A/p1765887862260529?thread_ts=1765803794.392969&cid=C05NYVA7T2A])

I did not mean my previous reply to be generic, so let me explain the thought in more detail.

Starting this October, our team started migrating all CS reports to New Generation Looker explores - [slack announcement|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CFN1NTKB5/p1761565639987449]. The idea is to build a new set of standard Looker reports that can be used by all CS teams. Yet we don’t just re-create previously existing dashboards, but rather build base reports that would cover all the daily needs of CS teams and be more universal, i.e., can be used for all verticals and/or for all markets.

So, for example, the Looker dashboard [MBR & WBR - CCPO & PRR|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/dashboards/20419?Case%2FOrder+Created+At+Timeframe=4+week+ago+for+4+week&Case+Vertical=Rides%2CUnknown&Country+Name=Kenya&Case+-+Customer+Support+Case+%28Yes+%2F+No%29=Yes&Time+Period=Week&Case+Created+At+Timezone=Created+%28UTC+timezone%29&Case+-+State=closed%2Csolved&Case+-+Outgoing+Case+%28Yes+%2F+No%29=No&Order+Created+At+Timezone=utc&PR+Created+At+Timezone=Created+%28UTC+timezone%29&Case+-+User+Persona=&Case+-+Safety+Related+%28Yes+%2F+No%29=&PR+-+Requested+Reason=-%22other_fraud%22&City=&Case+-+Case+Escalated+to+Agent+%28Yes+%2F+No%29=&Case+-+Is+Webview+Draft+%28Yes+%2F+No%29=No&Case+-+Issue+Title=&Case+Tier=] will be deprecated once we have new standard reports to cover all those data points - CCPO, Price Review volumes, Case volumes. Case volume trends can already be checked in the new set of Looker reports.

The new reports that are already available are:

* CSAT overview reports - [CSAT|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/folders/9184]
* Refunds & Compensation reports - [Refunds & Compensations|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/folders/9186]
* Customer Support Volumes reports - [Volumes|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/folders/9215]
* FRT overview reports - [FRT|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/folders/9190]
* Re-open Cases report - [Re-Opened Cases|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/folders/9225].

Thus, we will not adjust the currently existing Looker reports, but rather invest more effort and time into building new reports that would cover your needs.

For example, if you want to check the incoming volumes for delivery by week/month/quarter or by user persona or case issue, then you can already use [⭐️ Customer Support Volumes|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/dashboards/28358] and [⭐ Issue Keys Overview|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/dashboards/28535?4.%20Issue%20Key%20(Mandatory%20Field)=-NULL&Is%20Issue%20Key%20Active%20(Yes%20%2F%20No)=Yes&Issue%20Title=&User%20Persona=] Looker reports. They can be used to check the volume trends for any markets, any date period, and any vertical. Please go through them and see what is missing for you to solve your daily questions or tasks.

As for the CCPO per Issue - we are moving away from this as calculating CCPO per case issue is not the right approach; instead, we can see the volume trends and share of certain cases to total case volume - this will also give you an overview of what issue is prevailing in a market.

In order to ensure that new standard reports cover your needs, please go through the new reports listed above and share what is missing there and what questions you still have that cannot be answered with the new reports. Thank you in advance 🙏

Hello [~accountid:712020:ab95f96b-73f1-4bb8-a5fd-5178ef3f1339] and [~accountid:712020:011a9eb3-77af-4c62-bb26-e6c10e6097ec] I drafted a proposed response, however I would like to raise your attention to a *specific point of this PSP request, before we send the response.*

PSP requests “*_Workers' Compensation Insurance_*_:_ +_Mandatory for drivers, especially those who work as freelancers_+_, covering medical, surgical, pharmaceutical, and hospital expenses, as well as compensation for temporary or permanent disability, as established by Law No. 98/2009_.”

There are several aspects here that need to be addressed: 

h3. *1- PSP is quoting the wrong law.*

Law n.º 98/2009, of September 4, +does not relate to this insurance, but establishes a different type of insurance+. This law aims to regulate the system for compensation for occupational accidents and diseases, including vocational rehabilitation and reintegration, pursuant to Article 284 of the Labor Code.

This Law that they quote i+s only applicable within an employment relationship and this is not the relationship that exists between the Platform Operator and the Driver+. Therefore, this insurance is not applicable to Bolt. +If there was an employment relationship between the Driver and the Fleet, it would be the fleet’s obligation to have this type of insurance for their driver-employee+.

h3. *2- The insurance PSP is requesting actually exists, but in a different law.*

Decree-Law n.º 159/99, of May 11, establishes the obligation for +independent workers to have an insurance for work accidents+, that they need to contract for themselves.

h3. +*- Main issue for Bolt*+

Regarding insurance, the TVDE Law states, in article 12.º, n.º 6, that, *without prejudice to other insurance required by law*, TVDE vehicles must have +civil liability and personal accident insurance+, which includes passengers transported and their respective damages, in an amount not less than the legal minimum required for the activity of rental transport in light passenger motor vehicles.

We request the civil liability and personal accident insurance. However, the fact that the law says “_without prejudice to other insurance required by law_” raises the *question if we should be checking what other insurance types are legally required for TVDE drivers and vehicles and request those as well.*

However, establishing what kind of insurance a driver would need, between the 2 types mentioned above, +would depend on Bolt knowing what kind of relationship exists between the Driver and the Fleet+.

Even though article 10.º, n.º 2, e) of the TVDE Law establishes that +the driver must have a contract that regulates the relationship with the Fleet+ and article 14.º establishes that the +Platform Operator has the duty to verify compliance with all the requirements set forth in the law+, currently we do not perform this type of control, as *we do not request this contract*. Consequently, *since we have no knowledge on the relationship between Drivers and Fleets*, I believe *we are unable to determine what other kind of insurance would be required by law*.

h3. +*- Proposed Approach*+ 

Our position on this matter is that, even though this is a requirement stated by TVDE Law, *Bolt (or any Platform Operator) cannot force the Fleets and Drivers to have a contract between themselves or be responsible for evaluating their content, and this is not within the Platform’s capacity to enforce*.

Ideally, if you agree, I would prefer not raising PSP’s attention to any of these aspects. Hence I would prefer responding, regarding this matter, that the specific law they are quoting is not applicable in this case, without going into further details at this time.

h3. +- Question+

However, it would be important to know +if we have previously received any similar authority requests regarding this type of insurances+, or if this is the first time this issue is being raised.

* On 11 December, a Swedish rider ([profile|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/180850003/overview]) messaged Bolt CS ([here|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/702555947]) claiming that they had been hacked (as they have never been to Malmo).
** Rider claims that the phone number on the app is not theirs, and that “_Someone has taken my money_” (they have not provided further info / proof).
** On the same day, CS logged out all devices as a mitigation step.
* On 12 December, the rider again messaged CS ([here|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/703051600]) from a separate account under the same name ([profile|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/213736787/overview]) claiming that their Bolt account was linked to their previous phone number (+46763074484) and they can no longer log in as they do not have that phone number anymore. They claim that someone else is travelling with their money.
** Rider is adamant that “_I don't have access to the phone number, and someone else has my old number_”.
** Rider wants their bank card removed from the relevant account. It seems that they have blocked their card (“_I want you to refund me for the other trips after I wrote to you_ +_until I blocked my card_+”).
** Rider also wants to regain access to their old account.
* Unfortunately, CS have not been helpful, and have essentially prevented the rider from changing their bank details while also confirming that we cannot do it on our side. As such, the rider is understandably frustrated. Rider is threatening to go to the police.
* Based on internal investigation:
** [Account 1|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/180850003/overview]: 
*** Created under phone number +46763074484 in 2023. Email address is hotmail.
*** No recent account detail changes. However, new login via the phone number on 8 Dec 2025. This access is still ongoing.
*** Recent orders taken over the past week (8-12 December, 716kr/60eur total). Active mastercard on the account ending in 8985.
** [Account 2|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/213736787/overview]: 
*** Created under under phone number ending in 5629 in April 2024. Email address is gmail.
*** No recent account detail changes. 
*** No orders over the past month. No payment methods.

+*ANALYSIS*+

* This appears to be a case of phone number recycling. As such, it is a personal data breach.
** User 2 gained access to User 1’s account through use of a recycled phone number, and has used the payment method on the account to take trips, causing User 1 to suffer financial detriment of up to EUR 60.
** It appears that User 1 has blocked the card, so financial detriment is ongoing. However, unauthorised access is ongoing, and so must be addressed.
* I have reported this incident [here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C0678KJ49UH/p1765965613615429].

{quote}Hello Bolt user,

This can happen when mobile operators recycle phone numbers that are no longer in use - If a Bolt account remains linked to such a phone number and the phone number gets reassigned, the new owner may inadvertently gain access to the existing account, either when logging in or creating their own account.

Please note that, in accordance with our policies (in particular, to protect the data of the User and to ensure appropriate access control) we will be restoring the User’s access to the Account, which will mean that you will lose access to it.
